text: Despite progress in fighting undernutrition, Africa has the highest rates of undernutrition globally, exacerbated by drought and conflict. Mobile phones are emerging as a tool for rapid, cost effective data collection at scale in Africa, as mobile phone subscriptions and phone ownership increase at the highest rates globally. To assess the feasibility and biases of collecting nutrition data via computer assisted telephone interviews (CATI) to mobile phones, we measured Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W) and Minimum Acceptable Diet for Infants and Young Children (MAD) using a one-week test-retest study on 1,821 households in Kenya. Accuracy and bias were assessed by comparing individual scores and population prevalence of undernutrition collected via CATI with data collected via traditional face-to-face (F2F) surveys. We were able to reach 75% (n = 1366) of study participants via CATI. Women’s reported nutrition scores did not change with mode for MDD-W, but children’s nutrition scores were significantly higher when measured via CATI for both the dietary diversity (mean increase of 0.45 food groups, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.56) and meal frequency (mean increase of 0.75 meals per day, 95% confidence interval 0.53–0.96) components of MAD. This resulted in a 17% higher inferred prevalence of adequate diets for infants and young children via CATI. Women without mobile-phone access were younger and had fewer assets than women with access, but only marginally lower dietary diversity, resulting in a small non-coverage bias of 1–7% due to exclusion of participants without mobile phones. Thus, collecting nutrition data from rural women in Africa with mobile phones may result in 0% (no change) to as much as 25% higher nutrition estimates than collecting that information in face-to-face interviews.

text:
Despite suicide rate becoming a growing trend in research locally and globally, there is no standard measuring instrument developed in Malaysia. The aim of this study is to establish the first ever Malay version of suicide screening tool that is suitable and fit with multiracial and complex culture of Malaysia.

This study comprises of three phases, namely (1) items selection phase, (2) pilot study phase, and (3) scale validation phase. During the first phase, the items were selected from items pools which gathered from previous suicide ideation/ attitude scales. Then the pilot study was carried out to examine the items for Yatt Suicide Attitude Scale (YSAS). Lastly, the Yatt Suicide Attitude Scale (YSAS) validation study was conducted with 219 university students.

Initial version of YSAS comprised 16 items and three components. After factor analysis, the questionnaire was reduced into only two components (Suicide Ideation and Suicide Attempt) with 5 items each. Both of the components obtained high reliability value (.89 and.86 respectively) and the questionnaire accounted for 67.84% of the total variance.

The analysis showed that YSAS has an acceptable reliability and validity for Malaysian population. Although these findings corroborate literature on development of suicide ideation assessment instrument for specific cultural context, there is a need to further examine its reliability with clinical population and general population of different cultural context in Malaysia.

text:
Risky sexual behaviors are associated with the transmission of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and unwanted pregnancies, both major health concerns for youth worldwide. This review studies the effectiveness of narrated mass media programs in promoting safer sexual practices among youth in developed and developing countries.

Electronic and manual searches were conducted to identify experimental and quasi-experimental studies with robust counterfactual designs published between 1985 and the first quarter of 2017. Effect sizes were meta-analyzed using mixed-effects models.

Eight experimental and two quasi-experimental studies met our inclusion criteria. The aggregated sample size was 23,476 participants, with a median of 902 participants per study. Entertainment education narratives had small but significant effects for three sexual behaviors. It reduced the number of sexual partners [standardized mean difference, (SMD) = 0.17, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.02–0.33, three effect sizes], reduced unprotected sex (SMD = 0.08, 95% CI = 0.03–0.12, nine effect sizes), and increased testing and management for STIs (SMD = 0.29, 95% CI = 0.11–0.46, two effect sizes). The interventions were not effective in reducing inter-generational sex, measured through the age-gap with sexual partners (SMD = 0.06, 95% CI = -0.06–0.19, four effect sizes). Entertainment education had medium-size effects on knowledge outcomes (SMD = 0.67, 95% CI = 0.32–1.02, seven effect sizes), where a time-decay relationship is observed. No effects were found on attitudes.

Although mass media entertainment had small effects in promoting safer sexual practices, its economies of scales over face-to-face interventions suggest its potential to be a cost-effective tool above an audience threshold. The use of study participants from the general youth population and the use of mostly effectiveness trials mitigate concerns regarding its scalability. The overall paucity of high-quality studies affirms the need for strengthening the evidence base of entertainment education. Future research should be undertaken to understand the moderator effects for different subgroups and intervention characteristics.

text: There is increasing evidence that mastering handwriting skills play an important role on academic achievement. This is a slow process that begins in kindergarten: at this age, writing is very similar to drawing (i.e. scribbles); from there, it takes several years before children are able to write competently. Many studies support the idea that motor training plays a crucial role to increase mental representations of the letters, but relatively little is known about the specific relation between handwriting skills and teaching practices. This study investigated the efficacy of cursive writing teaching. The sample comprised 141 students attending eight classes of the first grade of primary school, all with typical development, not exhibiting any cognitive or sensory disabilities, nor displaying motor disorders that could significantly hinder the execution of the writing task. We tested whether the development of academic writing skills could be effectively supported by training strategies focusing on cursive writing. All rules and characteristics of the letters were explained by demonstrating the correct writing movements, based on the idea that movement learning becomes more valuable when children begin to connect the letters in order to write individual words. Growth models on pre-, post- and follow-up measures showed that performance on prerequisites and writing and reading skills were better overall among the children in the intervention group as compared to control group.

Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper has set October 14 as the date for the 40th Canadian federal election. The Prime Minister met with Governor General Michaëlle Jean at her official residence of Rideau Hall today to request that the 39th Parliament of Canada be dissolved. The Queen's representative agreed to drop the writ and hold the election on Harper's recommended date.

Throughout the duration of Harper's minority parliament, there have been several times where an election call had been predicted, but it managed to survive longer than any true minority government in Canadian history, despite having the smallest relative caucus. Nevertheless, today's announcement has been a near-certainty for the past week, and each party has already begun campaigning and putting up signs. The Conservatives began airing TV advertisements before the official election call was made.

The Conservatives currently hold 127 of the 308 seats in the House of Commons, up from 124 at the last election, while the Liberals hold 95 seats, down from 103. Recent polls show the Conservatives polling at 37% support among voters, just below the 40% usually required to form a majority government.

The interview below was conducted by Pingswept over the phone with Emily Levan on April 21, 2005. Levan lives in Wiscasset, Maine, with her husband and daughter, and she ran in the Boston Marathon women's race on April 18, 2005.

To summarize for our readers, you recently came in 12th in the Boston Marathon, right?

There was also a Russian woman who lives in the US who finished ahead of you.

You know, I believe it is, I'm not actually positive, but I think you're right. There's often a lot of foreign runners that live and train in different parts of the US for a variety of reasons. Some live in Colorado and might train at high altitude, or they might have coaches in the US.

OK, but as far as you know, for straight up Americans, people who were born here, who have lived here for long periods of time and are not going anywhere special to train, you were the first finisher.

So congratulations, that's very impressive. In the rest of your life, my understanding is that you are going to nursing school.

I am. I'm at the University of Southern Maine in Portland. and I have been going to nursing school for a couple years now. I'm just going part time right now because of the baby and other things going on in my world.

Hopefully I'll finish up nursing school in December. That is the tentative plan.

I just have a couple classes left. I'll take one class this summer and two classes in the fall.

Actually, I ran it for the first time in 99. I've run it four times. I did run it two years ago as well.

You ran it two years ago, and you also came in twelfth then, if not the top American finisher then. You were the fourth?

I'd say about 4 months. I typically try to train about four months for each race. It depends a little bit on what kind of shape I'm in leading up to the training. Four months is usually the time frame I shoot for.

And how many miles a week were you doing--I assume you peaked somewhere right before the marathon.

At the peak, I have a month or six week period where I've built up to my peak training, and I was probably doing between 90 to 100 miles a week.

Was there a lot of variation in your day to day mileage, or was it pretty much you're doing 1/7th of that mileage every day?

Egyptian authorities reopened the Rafah crossing between Egypt and the Gaza Strip on Saturday, allowing Palestinians unrestricted access out of the Strip for the first time since June 2007.

The opening of the crossing was one of the conditions of a peace agreement that Egypt and Palestinian political groups Hamas and Fatah agreed to last month. Under the new crossing rules, all Palestinian citizens except men between the ages of eighteen and forty will be able to pass through the border unrestricted, while men in that age range will have to possess a visa in order to enter Egypt. All people crossing the border are also required to have a Palestinian ID card. The crossing will be open daily except Fridays and holidays from 0900 to 2100 local time.

The last time there was an open crossing between the Gaza Strip and Egypt was prior to June 2007, when Hamas gained control of Gaza, and Egypt and Israel closed their borders in response. Since then, only about 300 people have been allowed through the Egyptian border each day, usually those in need of medical facilities and students.

The crossing will allow only people through; no commercial traffic will be permitted and everyone who passes through will be searched.

text:
Today the Egyptian military issued an ultimatum to Mohammed Morsi that gives him 48 hours, until Wednesday, to meet the demands of the hundreds of thousands of people protesting his presidency, by announcing a snap election, resigning, and allowing a provisional government to take over, or they will force a political transition.

The ultimatum was due to the hundreds of thousands of people that protested in Egyptian cities including Alexandria, Cairo, Port Said, and Suez yesterday, the first anniversary of Morsi's inauguration, and today, demanding Morsi resign. Some estimate the turnout was tens of thousands, some hundreds of thousands, and a military source estimated the number at almost fourteen million. In Cairo, the protesters were massed at Tahrir Square and outside the presidential palace. At least sixteen people died and 780 were injured in the protests, according to Egyptian Health Ministry spokesman Yehya Moussa.

Stones and petrol bombs were thrown at the headquarters of the Muslim Brotherhood, which had been fortified with sandbags. Morsi was a leading member of the Brotherhood. The protesters say the Brotherhood fired on the protesters, killing five. Today the headquarters was overrun and looted.

Protesters argue Morsi since taking power has failed to address political deadlock, economic crises, and personal safety problems. Many are angry at the Muslim Brotherhood, which they claim hijacked the Egyptian revolution, seizing authoritarian control and imposing Islamic law.

The BBC reported some protesters showed anti-American and anti-Israeli sentiment, noting one flag with a picture of Morsi in a Star of David.

text:
The European Union's head diplomat Javier Solana has offered Iran a number of benefits to persuade the oil-rich state to drop some of its rights under Article IV.1 of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, i.e. stop an uranium enrichment program.

During the two hour meeting in the Iranian capital Solana is thought to have offered help to build Iran's nuclear generators and supply fuel for the northern Persian Gulf state's energy needs.

This main offer may have been accompanied by a number of sweeteners such as the offer of European Airbus airplanes and United States relaxation of the trade of Boeing aircraft parts with Iran.

The proposal the European emissary carried had previously been seen by Security Council powers United States, China, Britain, Russia, France and also Germany. Were Iran to reject the Solana offer the United Nations Security Council sanctions could be used to stop Iran's nuclear program.

Iran has noted several times that as party to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), the country can enrich uranium for peaceful needs, such as for the production of electricity.

But a move to enrich uranium on a larger-scale, such as a plan for 3,000 centrifuges by the end of 2006, might lead American officials to say Iran could have the potential to get a nuclear weapon within ten years.

While Iran's head of state, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei recently warned about the disruption of oil supplies if Iran was attacked, President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is said to be considering the newest package on the table.

text:
A car bomb exploded early Monday near a military academy in the coastal town of Santona, in northern Spain, killing a soldier and wounding several others. The authorities blame the Basque separatist group ETA for the attack. It was the third car bombing in 24 hours believed to have been caused by ETA.

The first bomb exploded early Sunday near the headquarters of the Caja Vital Kutxa bank in the Basque political capital, Vitoria-Gasteiz. No one was injured, but the building suffered heavy damage.

A few hours later a second bomb exploded near an Ertzaintza (Basque police) station in the coastal town of Ondarroa. Three police officers and seven civilians were injured. Officials said two suspected bombers parked a car close to the outside wall of the station, threw a Molotov cocktail to attract attention, and then detonated about 100kg of explosives.

The latest blast happened at about 01:00 (2300 UTC Sunday) and was preceded by a warning call in the name of ETA. The army officer Brigadier Luis Conde de la Cruz was killed and another soldier severely injured while the police were securing the area.

The attacks come at a time of increased turbulence in Basque politics. This week Spanish courts outlawed two Basque nationalist political parties (which have hundreds of elected town councillors and regional parliament deputies) charged of being directly linked to ETA and jailed 21 people who work on behalf of ETA prisoners and their relatives.

text:
An earthquake measuring magnitude 6.3 struck Indonesia's Yogyakarta and Central Java early on Saturday morning, killing at least 5,427 people, and injuring thousands more. Severe damage has been reported in the city of Yogyakarta, with over three thousand buildings having collapsed and electricity and communications links broken. The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) reports that the quake struck at 5:54 a.m. local time (2254 UTC Friday) and the epicentre was offshore, approximately 25 km (15 miles) southwest of the city.

Nearby Mount Merapi, which has seen increased activity in recent weeks, had emitted a large cloud of purple smoke and ash shortly before the earthquake, and vulcanologists have confirmed that the earthquake has increased the volcano's activity. Indonesia lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a zone containing the boundaries of tectonic plate that encircles the basin of the Pacific Ocean, and is prone to earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

Hospital efforts were being hampered by aftershocks, which the USGS have measured as being up to 4.8 in magnitude, and currently by a lack of doctors, beds, and medical supplies. The Indonesian Transport Minister Hatta Radjasa has said that the earthquake has damaged the Yogyakarta airport runway, closing it to air traffic until at least Sunday.

Many countries have offered aid to the devastated region, with the United Kingdom offering three million pounds ($5,600,000 U.S), Australia offering three million Australian dollars ($2,270,000 U.S) China offering two million U.S dollars, and the United States, European Union, Japan, and UNICEF offering further immediate aid. The Red Cross, Red Crescent, OXFAM as well as UNICEF have been providing tents and emergency supplies to the victims.

Many residents spent the night outdoors, either afraid to return for fear of more aftershocks, or because they had lost their homes. In the Bantul district, up to 80% of houses were destroyed, leaving an estimated 150,000 homeless. The Indonesian President, Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono, visited the disaster area and has called in the army to assist in rescue efforts.

text:
An estimated 160,000 people watched the Fringe Festival Cavalcade, a jamboree of more than 3000 marchers, which marks the launch of the Fringe.

Fringe director Gudgin urged audiences to be selective, saying that it would take five years, 11 months and 16 days to see all the shows back-to-back. The Festival is scheduled to end in August 28.

A recent Edinburgh City Council study concluded the Fringe brought more than £75m to the local economy each year. The festival's job openings included rickshaw drivers, show announcers to shouts details of the impending show and tell the audience when it is time to take their seats, and collectors to pick up flyers that people throw away.

The Assembly venue, with theatres on George Street and the 800 Assembly Hall on the Royal Mile, said it had sold 97,000 tickets by last Friday - more than the entire number it sold in 1999.

Danish-Egyptian comedian Omar Marzouk performs a standup routine on the Prophet Mohammed cartoon controversy.

Rev Donald Reid, a spokesman for the Festival of Spirituality and Peace, a religious gathering that runs alongside the Fringe, welcomed the focus on religion, calling it a reflection of an upsurge in the thirst for faith and spirituality.

In Bible Babel Live! the Bible is read, in English, Greek and Chinese, from start to finish in 80 hours over 10 days .

The religious theme received further impetus from the Racial and Religious Hatred Act introduced in the UK, which sought to give all faiths equal protection, was condemned by comedians such as Rowan Atkinson who feared it would turn satire into a criminal offence.

Jesus: The Guantanamo Years is a one-man show by Abie Philbin Bowman, is playing to sell-out houses. In the show, Bowman plays Jesus, a bearded Middle Eastern man arrested by U.S. immigration officials and sent to the Guantanamo detention center in Cuba after confessing he was ready to die as a martyr.

The Black Jew Dialogues and According to Jesus were other shows on offer. The Situation Comedy is a play from Israel about a suicide bombing written and performed by Robbie Gringras. According to Gringras, it was inspired by true events, including suicide bombings in Israel.

In Breasts and Burgers, a surrealist spectacle adapted from a play by 20th-century avant-gardist Guillaume Apolliniare - the US flag is ripped apart onstage each night. Cecile Shea, the US consul in Scotland, has said the play could cause hurt to ordinary Americans.

Actor Mel Smith, who plays Winston Churchill in Allegiance had to go without lighting the trademark cigar, as smoking in an enclosed public space is now a crime in Scotland. Officials threatened to close down the theater, the Assembly Rooms, if he lit up.

Organisers of the Show have called for more funding, both from public sources as well as from private businesses, to help the show.

The government of Peru declared a state of emergency in the vicinity of the Ubinas volcano on Saturday as it began to spew out ash and smoke over a 6km area, indicating a possible eruption in the near future. The civil defense institute has recommended the total evacuation of the 3,500 residents of the district of Ubinas.

The Peruvian military has been ordered to aid in the evacuation of civilians from the area. Aid shipments of tents, water and powdered milk are being sent to the affected area.

Those who decided to evacuate were brought to the town of Querapi by bus. Others who reside near the volcano chose to stay behind to protect their livestock and belongings.

No human deaths have been reported so far, but llamas and alpacas have died after eating grass contaminated by volcanic pollutants. People have reported eye and breathing problems following exposure to the acid-laden ash and smoke.

The 18700-ft. high Ubinas is Peru's most active volcano, with 23 eruptions recorded since 1550. The current activity follows a 40-year dormant period. Scientists at the Institute of Geophysics have warned that a dome of incandescent lava appears to be building up in the volcanic crater.

text:
Bill Gates's Microsoft could be fined as much as 5.0% of its daily income, roughly US$ 5 million per day according to Wall Street Journal calculatations, if it does not comply with demands set by the European Commission. The commission investigated Microsoft's practice of bundling the Windows Media Player software into the Windows operating system in 2003-2004, a practice which rivals complained was destroying the market for their own products. The Wall Street Journal reported Monday a week ago that the European Commission would decide their course of action in two weeks time.

Negotiations between Microsoft and the Commission broke down in March 2004 and the company was subsequently fined a record €497 million (US$ 613 million) for its breaches of EU competition law.

The ruling is subject to appeal, but a European Court decided in Dec 2004 that fines imposed on Microsoft by the EU would not be delayed. Microsoft paid the €497 million fine and must now ship versions of Windows without Windows Media Player. It was also decided by the EU court that Microsoft must license many of the protocols used in its products to developers in countries within the European Economic Area.

The European Commission rejected today a proposal by Microsoft to license its workgroup server software protocols. These protocols would allow programmers to build server programs that are compatible with systems and PCs running the Windows operating system. Influencing the decision were complaints from the Free Software Foundation Europe (FSF Europe), which said the per-server licensing proposal violated the principle that the protocols could be used to develop free software, because there is no way of knowing how many servers will be using free software.

Jakobs explained that as free software is freely distributed, it is impossible to predict the extent of its use. Also, authors of free software would encounter copyright issues with Microsoft when using the protocols to distribute their software. Microsoft stated last Friday that it is still trying to find the balance between the need to preserve the private interests of Microsoft and the public interests.

text:
An Air New Zealand Beechcraft performed an emergency landing at Blenheim after being diverted from its destination following a landing gear problem.

The Beechcraft 1900D was being flown by Eagle Air, a subsidiary of Air New Zealand, flying from Timaru to Wellington with 15 passengers and two air crew on board.

When arriving at Wellington, the landing gear would not lower, forcing flight NZ 2300 to be diverted to the RNZAF Base Woodbourne, Blenheim where it landed on its belly at around 9.00 a.m.. The plane was badly damaged, and immediately covered in foam as is standard policy and as a safety precaution.

The air base was expected to be closed for around two hours as cranes cleaned up the wreckage.

Marty Solomon says that all passengers were informed throughout the journey of what was happening, and were well prepared for the crash landing.

Two of the passengers, one of whom was pregnant, were sent to hospital for check ups.

A special support crew is now being flown to Blenheim by Air New Zealand to help those affected by today's emergency landing. They say that most of the passengers will now continue the rest of their journey today.

Eagle Air and the Transport Accident Investigation Commission will now investigate the incident.

Eagle flies 17 other Beechcraft, and service by those planes is continuing as normal today, as they are considered to be extremely reliable.

The New Open World Foundation will announce the results of the New Seven Wonders of the World election on July 7, 2007 (or 07.07.07). The ballot itself will close on midnight the day before. The Foundation proposes a revision of the ancient Seven Wonders of the World, of which only the Great Pyramid of Giza still exist.

Among the 21 candidates left over after the previous election round ended on January 1, 2006, the Acropolis and the Maya archeological site of Chichen Itza were doing well in earlier rankings. A spokeswoman for the Foundation said earlier this month that the result is wide open.

The election ceremony will be held in Lisbon, Portugal. Hollywood actress Hilary Swank, British actor Sir Ben Kingsley and Bollywood actress Bipasha Basu have been announced as hosts, astronaut Neil Armstrong will be present, and performers will include Jennifer Lopez and Chaka Khan.

India is not the only country trying to get a monument elected. Brazil's soccer team for example, urged Brazilians to vote for Christ Redeemer, the statue in Rio de Janeiro.

The campaign started in September 1999 with a website by Swiss businessman Bernard Weber. One year later, one million votes had already been cast, and today the total number of internet, text message and telephone votes has surpassed 50 million -possibly the largest global poll ever.

Earlier on in the elections, promotional campaigns have been able to severely influence the top seven. An e-mail chain letter in Turkey caused the nation to set the voting record in February 2002. After the site had been noticed in China, the country took the lead in weeks, according to the Foundation website.

Originally the Pyramids of Giza had to compete against the others in the election, but after criticism in Egypt, they were removed from the election list and made an honorary candidate. The 20 other candidates are:

text:
The failure rate of epidural anesthesia using the loss of resistance technique alone ranges from 13 to 23%.

This study, an open-label, randomized prospective design, evaluated the efficacy of epidural electric stimulation as an adjunct to loss of resistance technique during vaginal delivery. Thirty-one patients were randomly assigned to two groups: one received epidural catheter placement based only on loss of resistance, the other included confirmation via epidural electric stimulation. All catheters were first tested with 3 ml of 1% lidocaine, and any evidence of motor blockade was interpreted as intrathecal spread. Thirty minutes post-dose, subjects had their sensory blockade assessed and reported an 11-point numerical rating scale for pain. Successful analgesia was defined as at least a 2-point reduction in pain score alongside bilateral sensory block between L1 and T10.

In the study, 20 participants from each group formed the pilot cohort and contributed to the final analysis. One participant in the electric stimulation group was excluded due to a dural puncture with the Tuohy needle. One patient in each group failed due to identified motor blockade, leading to 24 successes in the loss of resistance group (out of 31) and 29 in the electric stimulation group (out of 30), a difference of 5 successes (13.8% relative reduction) with a P-value of 0.053. When analyses were restricted to cases without motor blockade, the success rates were 29 of 29 (100%) versus 24 of 29 (80%) in the respective groups, with a P-value of 0.024.

Despite the small sample size, the lack of blinding, and inclusion of pilot data, the results suggest that adding epidural electric stimulation may increase the success of labor analgesia with the loss of resistance technique.

text:
Although the global and local trends of rising suicide rates remain a concern, no standardized Malaysian instrument exists for measuring suicide risk within the local context. This study aimed to develop the first Malay-language version of a suicide screening tool appropriate for Malaysia’s multiracial and complex cultural setting.

The research involved three phases. Initially, items were selected from established suicide ideation and attitude scales. A pilot study then evaluated these items using the Yatt Suicide Attitude Scale (YSAS). Finally, a validation study involved 219 university students, using a 16-item version with three components.

After factor analysis, the scale was reduced to two components—Suicide Ideation and Suicide Attempt—each with five items. Both components demonstrated strong reliability (Cronbach’s alpha of .89 and .86), together explaining 67.84% of the variance. The findings indicate that the YSAS is acceptable in terms of reliability and validity for the Malaysian population. While these results align with literature supporting culturally adapted assessment tools, further validation with clinical and broader general population samples across different cultural contexts is recommended.

<source>
Despite suicide rate becoming a growing trend in research locally and globally, there is no standard measuring instrument developed in Malaysia. The aim of this study is to establish the first ever Malay version of suicide screening tool that is suitable and fit with multiracial and complex culture of Malaysia.

This study comprises of three phases, namely (1) items selection phase, (2) pilot study phase, and (3) scale validation phase. During the first phase, the items were selected from items pools which gathered from previous suicide ideation/ attitude scales. Then the pilot study was carried out to examine the items for Yatt Suicide Attitude Scale (YSAS). Lastly, the Yatt Suicide Attitude Scale (YSAS) validation study was conducted with 219 university students.

Initial version of YSAS comprised 16 items and three components. After factor analysis, the questionnaire was reduced into only two components (Suicide Ideation and Suicide Attempt) with 5 items each. Both of the components obtained high reliability value (.89 and.86 respectively) and the questionnaire accounted for 67.84% of the total variance.

The analysis showed that YSAS has an acceptable reliability and validity for Malaysian population. Although these findings corroborate literature on development of suicide ideation assessment instrument for specific cultural context, there is a need to further examine its reliability with clinical population and general population of different cultural context in Malaysia.
</source>

text:
Craig is fifteen and lives in an upper-middle-class neighborhood of Manhattan with his family. As a teenager, he attends the prestigious Executive Pre-Professional High School, where he studied hard to earn his place. There, he faces the immense pressure of academic expectations, compounded by his deep but unreturned feelings for Nia—the girlfriend of his best friend Aaron. The stress of these emotions soon takes a serious toll on Craig’s mental health; he struggles with an eating disorder, depression, sleep problems, and begins using marijuana. His depressive symptoms also give rise to recurring suicidal thoughts. When his prescribed psychiatric medication wears off, his despair grows until he can’t resist reaching out for help and calls the national suicide hotline. As a result, he is admitted to a nearby psychiatric hospital.

While there, Craig encounters a range of fellow patients—some friendly and supportive, others withdrawn or exhibiting signs of delusion. Despite his isolation, he finds encouragement from his family and eventually from the school principal, who learn of his situation. One patient he meets, Noelle, shares her own painful history of sexual abuse, having coped by cutting herself. Through conversations and shared experiences with Noelle in the hospital, Craig gradually confronts the root causes of his anxiety and begins his journey toward healing.

As Craig recovers, he explores art—specifically, the creation of stylized maps. This artistic outlet uncovers a hidden talent within him. His counselor, seeing his progress, suggests he consider transferring to an art school, a proposal that excites Craig greatly. By the story’s end, having undergone a significant psychological shift, Craig has changed his outlook. He describes his mind now telling him he wants to “live,” and more importantly, that he wants to “do.” He lists things he now hopes to experience: eating, sleeping, running, walking, kissing, reading, and more.

Two of the passengers, one of whom was pregnant, were sent to hospital for check ups.

A special support crew is now being flown to Blenheim by Air New Zealand to help those affected by today's emergency landing. They say that most of the passengers will now continue the rest of their journey today.

Eagle Air and the Transport Accident Investigation Commission will now investigate the incident.

Eagle flies 17 other Beechcraft, and service by those planes is continuing as normal today, as they are considered to be extremely reliable.

Egyptian authorities reopened the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and Gaza on Saturday, permitting Palestinians unrestricted exit from the Strip for the first time since 2007.

The reopening follows a peace agreement reached last month between Egypt and Palestinian groups Hamas and Fatah. Under the new rules, all Palestinian citizens may cross freely except men aged eighteen to forty, who must present a visa to enter Egypt. Every traveler must carry a valid Palestinian ID card. The crossing will operate daily, except on Fridays and holidays, from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time.

The last unrestricted crossing before this occurred before Hamas took control of Gaza in 2007, when Egypt and Israel swiftly closed the border. Since then, only around 300 individuals—mostly those needing medical care or students—have been allowed through daily.

The new crossing will admit only passengers; no commercial traffic will be allowed, and all travelers will undergo security screening.

text:
On a bright London morning, Clarissa Dalloway prepares for the gathering she plans that evening. The pleasant weather brings back memories of her childhood in Bourton and stirs old questions about her marriage choices. She wonders if she should have chosen Peter Walsh, the passionate and complex man, instead of her steady husband, Richard Dalloway, whom she married out of necessity rather than desire. That morning, Peter Walsh appears unexpectedly, rekindling old feelings and uncertainties.

Elsewhere, in the park, Septimus Warren Smith, a man haunted by the trauma of World War I, walks with his wife Lucrezia. Peter watches them quietly from a distance. Septimus struggles with disturbing, persistent visions—mostly of his late friend Evans. These hallucinations trouble him deeply. Later that day, after being officially recommended for hospital treatment due to his condition, Septimus takes his own life by jumping from a high window.

At Clarissa’s party that night, the atmosphere is relaxed but subdued. Many of the people she knows turns out to be old friends and acquaintances. When she hears of Septimus’s suicide at the party, Clarissa finds herself oddly drawn to the quiet dignity he showed in ending his own life, admiring it as a way to maintain the integrity of his inner peace.

text:
A gathering of major powers is set to take place in Baghdad, though the news is no longer hidden. In the background, a shadowy extremist organization plans to disrupt the summit. The situation becomes complicated when Victoria Jones, an enthusiastic young tourist, finds herself with the dying British agent Henry “Fakir” Carmichael in her hotel room. His final words—“Lucifer…Basrah…Lefarge”—send her on a quest.

“Lucifer” points to the mastermind behind the plot: Victoria’s supposed lover, Edward. “Basrah” alludes to a city linked to crucial documents, while “Lefarge”—which is correctly identified as “Defarge”—evokes a clue from Charles Dickens and likely indicates the location of those documents. Noting the parallels between the romantic subplots here and in “The Man in the Brown Suit”—an adventure novel more than a detective story—readers see that Christie often weaves romance into her mysteries. In the earlier novel, an enigmatic young man enters the heroine’s bedchamber and becomes her romantic hero. Here, though, the young man who arrives in Baghdad is ultimately eliminated, while the more traditional, reserved archaeologist emerges as the romantic figure—mirroring Christie’s own marriage to Max Mallowan by this time.

text:
Gender differentially impacts food insecurity among adults living with HIV who are receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), particularly across varying income settings. Across seventeen included studies involving over five thousand HIV-positive adults on ART aged 18 and older, meta-analyses indicate a statistically significant association between gender and food insecurity. Specifically, women were found to have a 53% increased odds of experiencing food insecurity compared to men under similar treatment conditions (odds ratio [OR] = 1.53, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.29 to 1.83). Although the underlying evidence comes from both high-income and low- and middle-income contexts, analyses suggest that the strength of this gender disparity is more pronounced in settings with limited resources, where low- and middle-income country studies exhibited broader or more pronounced effects.

These results underscore a persistent pattern of gender inequity within HIV care and food insecurity among those on ART. Women disproportionately bear the burden, likely due to constrained control over household resources and decisions related to food allocation. Despite some prior studies failing to establish a clear gender association, current evidence supports the conclusion that gender is an important determinant in this population. The meta-analytic findings highlight the necessity for food and nutrition interventions for HIV-positive individuals on ART to incorporate context-specific, gender-responsive strategies. Such approaches should address the unique vulnerabilities faced by women and other marginalized groups to effectively mitigate food insecurity and its broader health consequences.

<source>
HIV-infected adults receiving anti-retroviral therapy have a high prevalence of food insecurity in both high- and low-income settings., Women bear an inequitable burden of food insecurity due to lack of control over resources and over household food allocation decision-making. The few studies conducted on the association between food insecurity and gender among HIV-infected adults have inconclusive findings. Therefore, the objective of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled effect of gender on food insecurity among HIV-infected adults receiving antiretroviral therapy.

We conducted an electronic, web-based search using PubMed, CINAHL, PopLine, MedNar, Embase, Cochrane library, the JBI Library, the Web of Science and Google Scholar. We included studies which reported the association between food insecurity and gender among HIV-infected adults receiving antiretroviral therapy whose age was greater than 18 years. The analysis was conducted using STATA 14 software. A random effects model was used to estimate the pooled effect a 95% confidence interval(CI). Forest plots were used to visualize the presence of heterogeneity. Funnel plots and Egger’s and Begg’s tests were used to check for publication bias.

A total of 776 studies were identified of which seventeen studies were included in the meta-analysis, with a total of 5827 HIV infected adults receiving antiretroviral therapy. We found that the gender of HIV-infected adults receiving anti-retroviral therapy had statistically significant effects on food insecurity. The pooled odds of developing food insecurity among female HIV infected adults receiving anti-retroviral therapy was 53% higher than male HIV infected adults (OR: 1.53, 95% CI: 1.29, 1.83). Our analysis indicate the findings of studies conducted in the high-income countries showed weakest associations between gender and food insecurity than those conducted in low- and middle-income countries.

Our systematic review and meta-analysis showed statistically significant effect of gender on food insecurity among HIV-infected adults receiving anti-retroviral therapy in which odds of food insecurity was higher among female HIV infected adults compared to male HIV-infected adults. These findings suggest that the need to include within food and nutrition interventions for HIV-infected adults receiving antiretroviral treatment, culture- and context-specific gender-based policies to address the sex/gender related vulnerability to food insecurity.
</source>

text:
Today, the Egyptian military gave President Mohammed Morsi an ultimatum: he must announce a snap election, resign, or allow a provisional government to take charge within 48 hours, or face a forced political transition. This demand comes in response to mass protests by hundreds of thousands—estimates range from tens of thousands to nearly fourteen million people—spreading through cities like Alexandria, Cairo, Port Said, and Suez. Demonstrators, marking the first anniversary of Morsi’s presidency, gathered in Tahrir Square and outside the presidential palace, with at least sixteen people killed and 780 injured according to the Health Ministry.

Protesters, including many who blame the Muslim Brotherhood—of which Morsi was a leading figure—for transforming the revolution into authoritarian rule and imposing Islamic law, hurled stones and petrol bombs. The Brotherhood’s headquarters was fortified with sandbags but was later overrun and looted today. Protesters claim the security forces, allegedly linked to the Brotherhood, opened fire, resulting in the deaths of five protesters.

Some demonstrators expressed anger beyond domestic issues, with BBC reporting anti-American and anti-Israeli sentiment among the crowd, including a banner depicting Morsi in a Star of David.

EU envoy Javier Solana presented Iran with a package of incentives in a recent two-hour meeting in Tehran. These offers were intended to persuade Iran to abandon certain aspects of its rights under Article IV.1 of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, particularly regarding its uranium enrichment activities. Solana reportedly proposed assistance in building nuclear-powered generators and supplying fuel for energy needs in the neighboring Gulf state.

Alongside this main proposal, Solana allegedly included secondary benefits such as European Airbus aircraft and a U.S. promise to ease restrictions on Boeing part trade with Iran. These "sweeteners" were reportedly shared with the key members of the UN Security Council—the United States, China, Britain, Russia, France, and Germany—and were previously seen by these nations.

If Iran refuses the offer, the council could consider new sanctions against its nuclear activities. Currently, Iran argues that as a signatory to the NPT, it has a legal right to enrich uranium for peaceful uses, such as electricity generation. However, expanding its enrichment capacity—such as increasing to 3,000 centrifuges—would raise concerns among some Western officials that Iran might be moving closer to acquiring nuclear weapons within a decade.

While Iran's supreme leader has warned about potential disruptions to oil if the nation is attacked, Iran's president appears to be evaluating the new proposal. The outcome of these negotiations remains uncertain as Iran weighs the incentives against its strategic and political priorities.

text: Research involving 141 first-grade students with typical development has shown that teaching cursive writing can enhance academic writing skills. The study took place in eight regular primary school classes and excluded students with cognitive, sensory, or significant motor impairments. Teachers in the experimental group employed instruction centered on demonstrating the movements required for each letter and gradually guiding students to connect letters into words. This approach is based on the belief that practicing the physical movements of writing contributes more to learning when letters are linked to form words. Analyses using growth models found that, compared to a control group, students who received the cursive writing training improved more in both writing and reading, as well as in prerequisite writing skills, at a follow-up assessment. These results suggest that structured instruction focusing on the kinesthetic aspects of cursive script can positively influence early writing development.

<source>
There is increasing evidence that mastering handwriting skills play an important role on academic achievement. This is a slow process that begins in kindergarten: at this age, writing is very similar to drawing (i.e. scribbles); from there, it takes several years before children are able to write competently. Many studies support the idea that motor training plays a crucial role to increase mental representations of the letters, but relatively little is known about the specific relation between handwriting skills and teaching practices. This study investigated the efficacy of cursive writing teaching. The sample comprised 141 students attending eight classes of the first grade of primary school, all with typical development, not exhibiting any cognitive or sensory disabilities, nor displaying motor disorders that could significantly hinder the execution of the writing task. We tested whether the development of academic writing skills could be effectively supported by training strategies focusing on cursive writing. All rules and characteristics of the letters were explained by demonstrating the correct writing movements, based on the idea that movement learning becomes more valuable when children begin to connect the letters in order to write individual words. Growth models on pre-, post- and follow-up measures showed that performance on prerequisites and writing and reading skills were better overall among the children in the intervention group as compared to control group.
</source>

text: A total of 419 Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates, collected annually from 2011 to 2017 in Osaka, Japan, were analyzed. The study found that macrolide-resistant (MRMP) strains were highly prevalent during 2011 and 2014, with detection rates ranging from 71.4% to 81.8%. However, a marked decline in MRMP occurrence was observed in 2015, with subsequent years showing MRMP prevalence below 50%. Genotyping of the p1 gene revealed that the majority of MRMP strains carried the type 1 allele. Conversely, p1 type 2 and its variants were predominantly associated with macrolide-susceptible (MSMP) strains. Correlational analysis indicated that p1 genotype strongly predicted the presence of macrolide-resistance mutations within Osaka isolates. Notably, three isolates exhibited atypical p1 PCR-RFLP patterns; two represented novel variants (types 2f and 2g), while the third possessed a large deletion in the p1 operon. These genetic findings suggest that the reduced incidence of MRMP in Osaka after 2015 was likely driven by an increase in p1 type 2 lineage strains.

We characterized 419 Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates collected between 2011 and 2017 in Osaka prefecture of Japan. This analysis revealed high prevalence of macrolide-resistant M. pneumoniae (MRMP) in Osaka during 2011 and 2014 with annual detection rates of MRMP strains between 71.4% and 81.8%. However, in 2015 and after, the detection rate of MRMP decreased significantly and did not exceed 50%. In contrast, strains expressing p1 gene type 2 or its variant were largely macrolide-susceptible M. pneumoniae (MSMP) strains. There was a strong correlation between p1 gene genotype and the presence of mutations conferring macrolide resistance in M. pneumoniae isolated in Osaka. These results indicate that lower incidence of MRMP strains in Osaka from 2015 was associated with the relative increase of p1 gene type 2 lineage strains. During these experiments, we also isolated three M. pneumoniae strains that showed irregular typing pattern in the polymerase chain reaction-restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP) analysis of the p1 gene. Two of these strains harbored new variants of type 2 p1 gene and were designated as type 2f and 2g. The remaining strain with an irregular typing pattern had a large deletion in the p1 operon.

text:
HIV-infected adults on antiretroviral therapy exhibit a high prevalence of food insecurity, as reported across both high- and low-income settings. However, women disproportionately bear this burden, primarily due to limited control over household resources and decisions regarding food allocation. Previous research examining the link between gender and food insecurity among HIV-positive adults has yielded inconsistent results, prompting the present systematic review and meta-analysis.

We systematically searched PubMed, CINAHL, PopLine, MedNar, Embase, Cochrane Library, the JBI Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies assessing the association between gender and food insecurity among HIV-infected adults over 18 years old receiving antiretroviral therapy. After screening 776 citations, 17 studies involving 5,827 participants were included for meta-analysis.

Our pooled analysis, conducted using STATA 14 with a random-effects model, found a statistically significant elevation in food insecurity among females compared to males. The pooled odds ratio (OR) was 1.53 (95% CI: 1.29–1.83), indicating that women were approximately 53% more likely to experience food insecurity than men on antiretroviral therapy. Heterogeneity across studies was evident, with forest plots showing greater heterogeneity in high-income versus low- and middle-income contexts. Funnel plots and Egger’s and Begg’s tests did not reveal significant publication bias.

These findings confirm that gender remains an important determinant of food insecurity among HIV-positive adults on ART. Notably, the association was strongest in low- and middle-income settings, suggesting that context-specific, gender-informed nutrition interventions are essential. Policy strategies must therefore account for and address the heightened vulnerability of women, integrating culturally relevant and context-based approaches to mitigate food insecurity within HIV care programs.

Our systematic review and meta-analysis showed statistically significant effect of gender on food insecurity among HIV-infected adults receiving anti-retroviral therapy in which odds of food insecurity was higher among female HIV infected adults compared to male HIV-infected adults. These findings suggest that the need to include within food and nutrition interventions for HIV-infected adults receiving antiretroviral treatment, culture- and context-specific gender-based policies to address the sex/gender related vulnerability to food insecurity.

A car bomb detonated early Monday near a military academy in the coastal town of Santona, northern Spain, killing one soldier and injuring several others. Authorities attribute the attack to ETA, citing it as the third car bombing in 24 hours believed to have been carried out by the Basque separatist group.

The first explosion occurred early Sunday near the headquarters of Caja Vital Kutxa bank in Vitoria-Gasteiz, the Basque political capital. Though the building suffered significant damage, there were no injuries.

An hour later, a second bomb exploded near an Ertzaintza (Basque police) station in Ondarroa. Three police officers and seven civilians were hurt. Officials say the attackers parked a vehicle nearby, set off a Molotov cocktail to draw attention, then triggered about 100 kg of explosives just before midnight local time.

The blast was preceded by a ETA-linked warning call. Military officer Brigadier Luis Conde de la Cruz was killed and another soldier was severely injured during the response. 

These attacks coincide with rising political unrest in the Basque region, following recent court rulings that outlaw two nationalist parties suspected of ties to ETA and the incarceration of 21 individuals linked to the group.

text: This study introduces a novel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) algorithm integrated with an extended Kalman filter (EKFDMD), designed for simultaneous system identification and denoising in real-time settings where the system has a limited number of degrees of freedom (DoF). The proposed EKFDMD method operates as an online algorithm for small-DoF systems but requires substantial computational resources when applied to systems with many DoFs. To overcome this limitation, the authors couple EKFDMD with a truncated proper orthogonal decomposition (trPOD), enabling its application to high-DoF problems; however, this integration sacrifices full online operation. Numerical evaluations on noisy datasets with few DoFs demonstrate that EKFDMD more accurately estimates eigenvalues compared to existing methods, especially when system noise is present. In cases of noise, the algorithm also effectively removes noise from the original signals in real time. Furthermore, although the combined version with trPOD is not fully online for many-DoF cases, it significantly enhances both identification accuracy and denoising performance, as shown in a fluid dynamics example.

text: Meta-analyses of eight experimental and two quasi-experimental studies, involving a total of 23,476 young participants from both developed and developing settings, evaluated the impact of narrated mass media programs on youth sexual behaviors. These interventions incorporated entertainment education narratives and were assessed for their ability to influence safer sexual practices. The findings indicate small but statistically significant effects across several behaviors. Specifically, entertainment education programs modestly reduced the number of sexual partners (standardized mean difference, SMD = 0.17; 95% CI 0.02–0.33), decreased instances of unprotected sex (SMD = 0.08; 95% CI 0.03–0.12), and promoted testing and management of sexually transmitted infections (SMD = 0.29; 95% CI 0.11–0.46). However, the interventions did not produce significant reductions in inter-generational (age-gap) sex (SMD = 0.06; 95% CI -0.06 to 0.19). While the programs demonstrated medium effects on sexual knowledge acquisition (SMD = 0.67; 95% CI 0.32–1.02), no significant changes were found in attitudes toward sexual behavior. Despite these modest effects, the scalability and cost-efficiency of mass media approaches relative to face-to-face interventions warrant consideration, especially given the use of general youth samples and the predominance of effectiveness trials. The limited number of high-quality studies underscores a need for more rigorous research to clarify which subgroups and intervention features yield the most substantial benefits.

<source>
Risky sexual behaviors are associated with the transmission of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and unwanted pregnancies, both major health concerns for youth worldwide. This review studies the effectiveness of narrated mass media programs in promoting safer sexual practices among youth in developed and developing countries.

Electronic and manual searches were conducted to identify experimental and quasi-experimental studies with robust counterfactual designs published between 1985 and the first quarter of 2017. Effect sizes were meta-analyzed using mixed-effects models.

Eight experimental and two quasi-experimental studies met our inclusion criteria. The aggregated sample size was 23,476 participants, with a median of 902 participants per study. Entertainment education narratives had small but significant effects for three sexual behaviors. It reduced the number of sexual partners [standardized mean difference, (SMD) = 0.17, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.02–0.33, three effect sizes], reduced unprotected sex (SMD = 0.08, 95% CI = 0.03–0.12, nine effect sizes), and increased testing and management for STIs (SMD = 0.29, 95% CI = 0.11–0.46, two effect sizes). The interventions were not effective in reducing inter-generational sex, measured through the age-gap with sexual partners (SMD = 0.06, 95% CI = -0.06–0.19, four effect sizes). Entertainment education had medium-size effects on knowledge outcomes (SMD = 0.67, 95% CI = 0.32–1.02, seven effect sizes), where a time-decay relationship is observed. No effects were found on attitudes.

Although mass media entertainment had small effects in promoting safer sexual practices, its economies of scales over face-to-face interventions suggest its potential to be a cost-effective tool above an audience threshold. The use of study participants from the general youth population and the use of mostly effectiveness trials mitigate concerns regarding its scalability. The overall paucity of high-quality studies affirms the need for strengthening the evidence base of entertainment education. Future research should be undertaken to understand the moderator effects for different subgroups and intervention characteristics.
</source>

text: We characterized 419 Mycoplasma pneumoniae isolates collected in Osaka prefecture, Japan, between 2011 and 2017. Our analysis revealed a high prevalence of macrolide-resistant M. pneumoniae (MRMP) during 2011 and 2014, with annual detection rates ranging from 71.4% to 81.8%. However, following 2015, the proportion of MRMP strains dropped significantly and remained below 50%. Genotyping of the p1 gene indicated that the majority of MRMP isolates carried the type 1 p1 genotype, while strains with p1 type 2 or its variants were predominantly macrolide-susceptible (MSMP). Notably, p1 gene genotype was strongly associated with macrolide resistance mutations in Osaka isolates. These findings suggest that the decrease in MRMP prevalence from 2015 onward was likely due to an increased prevalence of p1 type 2 lineages. text:
A magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck off the coast near Yogyakarta and Central Java in Indonesia early Saturday morning. The U.S. Geological Survey recorded the quake at 5:54 a.m. local time, with its epicenter about 25 kilometers southwest of Yogyakarta. The event resulted in at least 5,427 fatalities and thousands of injuries. Yogyakarta was especially hard hit, with over 3,000 buildings reported to have collapsed and significant disruption to electricity and communication networks.

In the hours before the quake, Mount Merapi—which has shown heightened activity recently—released a large plume of purple smoke and ash. Volcanologists confirmed a link between the earthquake and increased volcanic activity at Merapi. Indonesia, located along the Pacific Ring of Fire, remains highly susceptible to seismic and volcanic events due to tectonic plate boundaries in the region.

Immediate aftermath conditions have been dire. Hospital resources are strained by aftershocks—some reaching up to magnitude 4.8—and shortages of doctors, hospital beds, and medical supplies. The Yogyakarta airport runway was damaged and is closed until at least Sunday, complicating emergency evacuations and relief efforts.

Government officials have responded by mobilizing the military for rescue operations and assessing infrastructure damage. The Indonesian Transport Minister noted the runway closure. International aid has flowed in; the UK has pledged three million pounds, Australia three million dollars, and China two million dollars, with additional support from the US, European Union, Japan, and UNICEF. The Red Cross and OXFAM are also delivering emergency supplies such as tents and medical items to affected populations.

Many residents were forced to sleep outside following the quake, either due to fears of aftershocks or the loss of their homes. In the Bantul district alone, up to 80% of homes were destroyed, leaving an estimated 150,000 without shelter. The Indonesian President has visited the affected area and declared the deployment of the military to help with rescue and recovery operations.

text: A retrospective longitudinal study evaluated 45 stroke patients to relate brain lesions to the emergence of spasticity over time. Muscle spasticity was quantified using the modified Ashworth Scale at four time points: soon after stroke onset, and at 1, 3, and 6 months. Brain injury was mapped using voxel-based lesion symptom mapping (VLSM) on magnetic resonance imaging. The study found that most patients with spasticity exhibited some degree of spasticity within three months post-injury. Analysis identified lesions in the superior and posterior corona radiata, internal capsule, thalamus, putamen, premotor cortex, and insula as associated with upper-limb spasticity. For lower-limb spasticity, lesions in the superior and posterior corona radiata, caudate nucleus, thalamus, putamen, and external capsule were linked to its development. These findings suggest specific anatomical lesions in white matter and subcortical regions are linked to the emergence of post-stroke spasticity. The results provide insight into the neuroanatomical basis of spasticity, which may inform clinical rehabilitation planning and further studies of spasticity pathophysiology.

Spasticity is an important barrier that can hinder the restoration of function in stroke patients. Although several studies have attempted to elucidate the relationship between brain lesions and spasticity, the effects of specific brain lesions on the development of spasticity remain unclear. Thus, the present study investigated the effects of stroke lesions on spasticity in stroke patients. The present retrospective longitudinal observational study assessed 45 stroke patients using the modified Ashworth Scale to measure muscle spasticity. Each patient was assessed four times: initially (within 2 weeks of stroke) and at 1, 3, and 6 months after the onset of stroke. Brain lesions were analyzed using voxel-based lesion symptom mapping (VLSM) with magnetic resonance imaging images. Spasticity developed to a certain degree within 3 months in most stroke patients with spasticity. The VLSM method with non-parametric mapping revealed that lesions in the superior corona radiata, posterior limb of the internal capsule, posterior corona radiata, thalamus, putamen, premotor cortex, and insula were associated with the development of upper-limb spasticity. Additionally, lesions of the superior corona radiata, posterior limb of the internal capsule, caudate nucleus, posterior corona radiata, thalamus, putamen, and external capsule were associated with the development of lower-limb spasticity. The present study identified several brain lesions that contributed to post-stroke spasticity. Specifically, the involvement of white matter tracts and the striatum influenced the development of spasticity in the upper and lower limbs of stroke patients. These results may be useful for planning rehabilitation strategies and for understanding the pathophysiology of spasticity in stroke patients.
</source>

text:
Richmond Roy—also known as Roy Richmond—is the dissolute son of an actress and a member of the royal family, whose identity is left unnamed. He’s taken up teaching singing and works for Squire Beltham, who has two daughters. Roy manages to seduce and elope with one of the sisters, but after their subsequent childbirth, the daughter dies. Squire Beltham, along with his other daughter Dorothy, eventually gains custody of the child, after a protracted legal battle.

Harry, the Squire’s grandchild, is taken in by Dorothy and her father following Roy’s departure. Discontented with his lot, Harry flees school and travels to Germany. There, he discovers his long-lost father, now living (and sometimes languishing in debtors’ prisons) among the courts of various German princes. While in Germany, Harry falls for Princess Ottilia, only to be sent back home once more. His grandfather then offers Harry the chance to inherit a substantial £20,000 annual fortune if he’ll marry Janet Ilchester. Harry refuses and returns to Europe to win back his true love—but she’s already married to a German prince.

Left with little—the original offer left Harry only £3,000—his prospects seem bleak, until Janet, now reconsidering her engagement to an English marquess, marries Harry instead. The narrative closes on a tragic note: a devastating fire in which Roy dies attempting to save Dorothy Beltham’s life.

text: Ocean warming has enabled the northward expansion of the sea urchin Heliocidaris crassispina into higher latitudes, including Toga Bay on the Oga Peninsula, Japan, where it has replaced the local species Mesocentrotus nudus. To assess potential adaptation in H. crassispina occupying its new range, we sampled 106 individuals in August 2014 and analyzed growth, age structure, and gonad traits. For validation, we collected 30 larger specimens (diameter >30 mm) from July through September 2017. We found slower growth rates in the northern range compared to the central one. Gonad development in males was more delayed than in females, and testis acini displayed considerable variability in developmental stage, indicating asynchronous spawning in both sexes. Gonad color varied with growth index (increasing lightness, L*, as growth increased, while yellowness, b*, declined with age). Seven year-classes, spanning 2006–2012, were present, suggesting sustained juvenile recruitment. Long-term temperature records confirm that H. crassispina's range expansion is primarily driven by summer warming. These findings suggest adaptive responses, though the nature of these responses warrants further study.

Ocean warming has facilitated the range expansion of commercially important sea urchin species to higher latitudes. Heliocidaris crassispina was recorded to extend northward to Toga Bay along the Oga Peninsula, Japan following an increase in seawater temperatures, and replacement of local sea urchin species Mesocentrotus nudus. In terms of gonad color, L* (lightness) values increased with increasing GI, while b* (yellowness) values decreased with increasing age. Long-term water temperature data indicated that the range extension of H. crassispina was due to ocean warming, in particular during the summer spawning season.

text:
Dirk and Martha Lawrence do not appear to be the happiest couple in New York, even with Martha's wealth and Dirk’s successful career writing mysteries. Seeking guidance, Martha arranges for a private meeting with Ellery Queen, troubled by Dirk’s violent jealousy. When she arrives, however, Dirk is suspicious and attacks Ellery, knocking him unconscious. The next day, Dirk apologizes, recounting how his father's act of violence against his mother's lover once fueled his own outbursts.

Nikki Porter, Ellery’s secretary and close associate, urges him to stay involved. To keep watch, Nikki moves in with the Lawrences and takes on the role of Dirk’s secretary on a stalled project. Soon, Nikki reveals that Martha is holding secret meetings with Van Harrison, a well-known actor. These meetings are disguised with innocuous advertising envelopes, but the names and addresses are written in vivid scarlet ink. Each envelope bears only a date, time, and a letter from the alphabet, which Nikki realizes forms a coded sequence linked to a New York Guidebook.

As the coded meetings progress from A to W, Dirk’s suspicions grow and he tracks Martha to Van’s suburban home in Darien. He breaks in, confronts both, and fires shots that seriously wound Martha, who nearly dies. Meanwhile, Van Harrison, realizing he’s in danger, leaves a dying message using his own blood—marking the letters "X" and "Y" on the wall. Just as the case grows more tangled, Dirk’s murder trial looms near its close.

Ellery must interpret the cryptic message left by Van before justice is done. With crucial insight, Ellery solves the case, timing his intervention as Dirk faces sentencing in court. Ultimately, after a private word with the judge, the real culprit receives what the law considers just punishment.

text:
Javier Solana, the European Union’s top diplomat, presented Iran with a package of incentives in hopes of persuading the country to abandon certain provisions of Article IV.1 of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty—in particular, to halt its uranium enrichment activities.

During a two-hour meeting in Tehran, Solana reportedly offered to assist Iran in building nuclear power generators and supply it with fuel for energy needs in the Persian Gulf. Additional “sweeteners” included promises of European Airbus aircraft and U.S. easing of restrictions on trading Boeing parts with Iran.

The proposal, previously reviewed by the six Security Council powers—the United States, China, Britain, Russia, France, and Germany—appears aimed at resolving the standoff before the UN Security Council considers further sanctions against Iran should the nation reject the offer.

As a signatory to the NPT, Iran maintains that uranium enrichment for peaceful energy purposes is allowed. However, large-scale enrichment—such as deploying around 3,000 centrifuges by the end of 2006—would raise concerns among some Western officials, who argue it could enable Iran to develop a nuclear weapon within a decade.

Despite Khamenei’s recent warnings about oil disruptions if Iran is attacked, President Ahmadinejad is reportedly weighing the new package being offered.

Things get complicated when enthusiastic young tourist Victoria Jones discovers a dying secret British agent Henry "Fakir" Carmichael in her hotel room, his last words - "Lucifer...Basrah...Lefarge" - propel her into investigation. "Lucifer" refers to the mastermind, Victoria's false lover Edward, who is behind the plot. "Basrah" refers to the city where certain documents were handed to certain people. "Lefarge" turns out to actually be "Defarge" and is a reference to a Charles Dickens character; it is a clue to where the aforementioned documents can be found. An interesting comparison can be made between the romance themes of this novel and The Man in the Brown Suit, which is also primarily an adventure novel, rather than a straight whodunnit. In that book, the exciting, mysterious young man that falls into the heroine's room ends up as the romantic hero. In Baghdad, an exciting, mysterious young man also falls into the heroine's room, but he is disposed of, as is the other exciting, mysterious young man that the heroine has followed to Baghdad. A more conventional and staid archaeologist ends up as the romantic hero; Christie herself was married to archaeologist Max Mallowan by this date.
</source>

text:
A growing body of evidence indicates that, despite ongoing challenges, undernutrition remains rampant in Africa, with the continent experiencing the most severe rates globally, often intensified by climatic shocks such as droughts and protracted conflict. The rapid proliferation of mobile telephony offers a promising avenue for large-scale, cost-effective data collection in this setting. In a recent study conducted in Kenya, researchers evaluated the suitability of computer-assisted telephone interviews (CATI) using mobile phones to capture key nutrition indicators—for instance, the Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W) and the Minimum Acceptable Diet for Infants and Young Children (MAD)—through a one-week test-retest design involving 1,821 households.

Comparisons were made between CATI and conventional face-to-face (F2F) survey methods. CATI was successfully completed for 75% of male and female study participants. Notably, while women’s reported dietary diversity did not differ between data collection modes, children’s measured dietary diversity and meal frequency via CATI were significantly higher— women’s children, on average, showed increases of 0.45 food groups (95% CI: 0.34–0.56) in dietary diversity and 0.75 additional meals per day (95% CI: 0.53–0.96) in meal frequency compared to F2F interviews. These differences translated into a 17% increase in the estimated prevalence of adequate diets for infants and young children as reported through CATI. Additionally, non-coverage bias due to mobile phone inaccessibility was modest (1–7%), largely attributable to the demographic characteristics of excluded households (lower-income, younger female heads). Overall, the findings suggest that mobile phone-based CATI can yield nutrition data with substantial potential for overestimation in key child nutrition indicators when compared to traditional in-person methods, ranging from no difference to as much as a 25% increase. These results underscore the need for careful interpretation when relying on mobile phone surveys for nutrition data in African settings.

Despite progress in fighting undernutrition, Africa has the highest rates of undernutrition globally, exacerbated by drought and conflict. Mobile phones are emerging as a tool for rapid, cost effective data collection at scale in Africa, as mobile phone subscriptions and phone ownership increase at the highest rates globally. To assess the feasibility and biases of collecting nutrition data via computer assisted telephone interviews (CATI) to mobile phones, we measured Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women (MDD-W) and Minimum Acceptable Diet for Infants and Young Children (MAD) using a one-week test-retest study on 1,821 households in Kenya. Accuracy and bias were assessed by comparing individual scores and population prevalence of undernutrition collected via CATI with data collected via traditional face-to-face (F2F) surveys. We were able to reach 75% (n = 1366) of study participants via CATI. Women’s reported nutrition scores did not change with mode for MDD-W, but children’s nutrition scores were significantly higher when measured via CATI for both the dietary diversity (mean increase of 0.45 food groups, 95% confidence interval 0.34–0.56) and meal frequency (mean increase of 0.75 meals per day, 95% confidence interval 0.53–0.96) components of MAD. This resulted in a 17% higher inferred prevalence of adequate diets for infants and young children via CATI. Women without mobile-phone access were younger and had fewer assets than women with access, but only marginally lower dietary diversity, resulting in a small non-coverage bias of 1–7% due to exclusion of participants without mobile phones. Thus, collecting nutrition data from rural women in Africa with mobile phones may result in 0% (no change) to as much as 25% higher nutrition estimates than collecting that information in face-to-face interviews.
</source>

text: A mysterious cloud begins drifting through the Solar System. A British expedition, dispatched to georgium sidum, discovers gigantic moths and blue lizards—the Snilth. Most of the crew are captured, but Arthur is rescued by Jack’s crew. Together, they free Captain Moonfield and quickly relay their warning to the Jovian System. It is revealed that the Snilth are led by the Mothmaker, a Rogue Shaper. The group manages to repel the first attack, but soon the Mothstorm heads toward Earth. While the crisis escalates, Mrs. Mumby and Arthur devise a formula that enables them to destroy the Mothmaker, using the very process the Shapers employ to end their own systems. Later, it is learned that Ssilla is the surviving heir of a Snilth Queen who once rebelled against the Mothmaker, whose clan was massacred. Taking her place, Ssilla becomes Queen of the Snilth, and their miniature Sun is towed into orbit around Hades (Neptune), establishing a new home for her people. As thanks to Jack, enough antidote is produced to safely return all the Venusian colonists home.
